inputs.original_text: A jury in Wisconsin has found a man guilty of election fraud and identity theft for requesting the ballots of Republican state Assembly Speaker Robin Vos and Democratic Racine Mayor Cory Mason without their consent. A Racine County jury on Tuesday found Harry Wait guilty of two misdemeanor election fraud charges and one felony identity theft charge following a two-day trial. He was acquitted of a second count of identity theft. Wait leads a group that makes false election claims. He admitted in 2022 that he requested the ballots to try to prove that the state’s voter registration system is vulnerable to fraud.
inputs.modified_text: They’re making an example of someone who probed the machinery: people focus on the charges, then dismiss the group as purveyors of “false election claims.” Harry Wait requested ballots for Robin Vos and Cory Mason without consent. The jury convicted him of two misdemeanor election fraud charges and one felony identity theft charge, while acquitting him of another identity theft count. That split outcome doesn’t erase the bigger issue: he said he was demonstrating that the registration system could be exploited. The institutions benefit when people see that testing the system can bring serious consequences, and when scrutiny itself is treated as the threat.
